transcript: It’s always exciting when an old play feels remarkably alive in the present. This is how I felt about Wine In The Wilderness at Classic Stage. This play by Alice Childress is set in an apartment in 1964 while a riot rips through the streets of Harlem outside. A painter named Bill intends to complete his series on Black womanhood, and his friends have found him his third and final subject. She doesn't end up being who they all thought she was — she's much more complex than they were giving her credit for, to say the least. This is a play about challenged assumptions and a resistance to prescribed roles and archetypes, all in the name of community and our individual humanity. I thought this was a really great production. All the design elements and the direction by LaChanze are detailed and natural, and there's a wonderful ease and resonance exuding from all the actors in their delivery of this truly fantastic, insightful, and poetic script. Wine In The Wilderness is running through April 13th under Classic Stage Company. With that, another program for my collection.
